sentences.label: Lowering the risk
sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the risk: being a woman takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 18% to below 1% and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 8%; through this sum alone, compared with no chest pain symptoms, typical angina or non-anginal chest pain lowers it to about 2% and atypical angina to about 5% (chest pain type also acts through the parts below).

sentences.label: Raising the risk
sentences.text: A reversible defect (or the undefined code 4) on the thallium scan raises it to about 55%; higher cholesterol (from about 8% at 193 mg/dL to about 45% at 308 mg/dL), higher resting blood pressure (from about 9% at 110 mm Hg to about 35% at 155 mm Hg) and older age (from about 10% at 42 years to about 25% at 66 years) raise it steadily.

Through this sum alone, each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same (from about 18% at 0 to about 80% at 2 vessels) and a flat ST segment raises it to about 87%, while the maximum heart rate barely changes it; all three also act through the parts below.

sentences.label: Rare results
sentences.text: Rarer results also count (the model has little data on this, n = 15 and 17): a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers the risk to about 3%, and through this sum alone a downsloping ST segment raises it to about 32%; the model ignores exercise-induced angina.

This part combines chest pain type with the number of vessels coloured: through it, typical angina lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 18% to about 2%, and each extra vessel adds about the same, from about 18% at 0 to about 61% at 2 vessels.

Across the whole model, more vessels raise the predicted risk, and even more so with typical angina, each extra vessel adding about the same: going from 0 to 2 vessels moves a typical patient from below 1% to about 55% with typical angina, and from about 18% to about 99% with any other chest pain type.
Across the whole model, typical angina takes a typical patient's predicted risk to below 1%.

This part combines the resting ECG with ST depression on exercise and acts on 42 of 242 training patients, nearly all with a normal resting ECG, 26 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 98% without it and about 99% with it.

Through it, more ST depression raises the predicted risk only once it rises above about 1.0 mm, for patients with a normal resting ECG, in an uneven way: for a typical such patient from about 13% at 0 mm to about 63% at 3.5 mm.

More ST depression therefore raises the predicted risk, but only if the resting ECG is normal: going from 0 to 2.8 mm moves a typical patient from about 18% to about 55% with a normal resting ECG, in an uneven way, and leaves it at about 18% otherwise.

This part combines the number of vessels coloured with a flat ST segment: through it, each extra vessel adds about the same, from about 18% at 0 to about 36% at 2 vessels for a typical patient, and a flat ST segment raises the risk from about 18% to about 23%.

Across the whole model, each extra vessel takes a typical patient from about 18% at 0 to about 99% at 2 vessels, about the same for each, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher, and a flat ST segment takes it to about 91%.
This part reads only non-anginal chest pain: through it, non-anginal chest pain lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 18% to about 8%.
Across the whole model, non-anginal chest pain takes it to about 1%.

This part reads only the maximum heart rate: a higher maximum heart rate lowers the predicted risk with nothing until about 145 beats per minute, then steadily, for a typical patient from about 19% at 118 to about 14% at 175 beats per minute.
Across the whole model the same holds, from about 19% at 118 to about 14% at 175 beats per minute.

lead.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results) the model predicts a risk of heart disease of about 18%; it adds up most of its inputs independently, and five parts add to that sum: two add more for each extra vessel coloured, one lowers the risk for typical angina, one lowers it for non-anginal chest pain, one acts only on the 42 of 242 training patients with a normal resting ECG and marked ST depression, and one lowers it for a higher maximum heart rate, with nothing until about 145 beats per minute, then steadily.

Its formula reproduces the part exactly on all 242 training patients.

parts.name: heart_disease_logit
parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: the heart-disease logit is essentially a logistic regression. 13 direct input->output edges (largest: sex:0 -1.87, slope:2 +1.72, ca +1.30, cp:4 +1.25, chol +0.93, thal:3 -0.87, thal:6 -0.86, trestbps +0.67, cp:2 +0.44, age +0.40, fbs:1 -0.32, slope:3 +0.20, thalach +0.002) are added to five children: ca_slope2_relay and the 2245 relay (raise the effective ca weight to 2.60 per SD), cp3_relay (non-anginal pain lowers risk), st_depression_normal_ecg_gate (ST depression raises risk only with a normal resting ECG), typical_angina_ca_switch's 3210 (typical angina lowers risk, less with more vessels) and max_heart_rate_hinge (small). Nine inputs are unconnected (sex:1, fbs:0, restecg:1, restecg:2, exang:0, exang:1, slope:1, thal:4, thal:7): exercise-induced angina is ignored. Evidence (train, n=242): AUC 0.9392; all hidden units replaced by their best linear fits 0.9355 (= L2 logistic regression 0.9355); all ReLUs as identity 0.9078; all hidden mean-ablated 0.9241. The gain over linear (+0.0037) comes from the ECG/ST gate (+0.0034 restored alone), the heart-rate hinge (+0.0008) and the typical-angina switch (+0.0003); the relays contribute none. Direct edges carry logit SD 4.25 of 5.63.

parts.name: typical_angina_ca_switch
parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: (i) node 2245 = ReLU(0.578 ca + 1.276) is an always-on ca relay adding +0.88 logit per SD of ca (output weight 1.528); (ii) node 3210 = ReLU(0.901 cp:1 - 0.644*2245 + 0.420) is a typical-angina switch: it is on only for cp:1 patients and then lowers the logit by 0.833 x its activation, from about -2.26 at the lowest ca (-0.73 SD) to about -1.22 at the highest ca (2.64 SD). So typical angina lowers predicted risk, and the reduction shrinks with more narrowed vessels. Evidence (train, n=242): 2245 never clips (0.86..2.80); 3210 active for all 22 cp:1 patients and none of the 220 others. Mean ablation AUC 2245 0.9339, 3210 0.9354; linear replacement 0.9392 / 0.9391 (3210 is a cp:1 switch whose within-group response is linear in ca).

parts.name: st_depression_normal_ecg_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: node 1801 = ReLU(1.542 restecg:0 + 0.817 oldpeak - 1.521) is a gate in which ST depression (oldpeak) raises predicted risk only for patients with a normal resting ECG (restecg:0), once oldpeak is above about its mean (threshold -0.03 SD); with an abnormal resting ECG the threshold is 3.75 SD and the gate is effectively closed. Evidence (train, n=242): active for 41 of 121 normal-ECG patients and 1 of 121 others; adds 1.40 x activation = +1.14 logit per SD oldpeak when open. It is the model's main nonlinearity: mean ablation AUC 0.9339, linear replacement 0.9362, and restoring it onto the all-linear model gains +0.0034 AUC. oldpeak has no direct edge, so the model ignores ST depression for patients with an abnormal resting ECG.

parts.name: ca_slope2_relay
parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: node 664 = ReLU(0.456 ca + 0.185 slope:2 + 0.783) is an affine relay that strengthens the direct ca and flat-ST-slope (slope:2) effects. Evidence (train, n=242): pre-activation 0.28..2.19, never clips, so the part is exactly affine on the data; it adds +0.42 logit per SD of ca and +0.17 per SD of slope:2 (output weight 0.92). Mean ablation AUC 0.9392 -> 0.9375; linear replacement leaves AUC at 0.9392. No concept beyond reweighting.

parts.name: max_heart_rate_hinge
parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: a small hinge on maximum heart rate (thalach). Node 2009 = ReLU(0.833 thalach + 0.201) feeds the output (-0.151) and the always-on relay 2650 = ReLU(0.982*2009 + 0.859) (-0.172), a net -0.32 x 2009: higher maximum heart rate lowers predicted risk, but only above about -0.24 SD; below that it has no effect (the direct thalach edge, +0.002, is negligible). Evidence (train, n=242): 2009 active for 64% of patients; logit contribution SD 0.16 (small); mean ablation AUC 0.9391, linear replacement 0.9392, restore-onto-linear gain +0.0008.

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients

ann_29.text: Through this part, the model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 18% at 0 vessels to about 36% at 2 vessels (on the training data only).

Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 23%) than if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than a flat ST segment (about 18%) (on the training data only).

ann_30.text: Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a lower predicted risk of heart disease if the patient has non-anginal chest pain (about 8%) than if chest pain type is something other than non-anginal chest pain (about 18%) (on the training data only).

ann_31.text: This part acts on 42 of 242 training patients (17%); nearly all of them are patients with a normal resting ECG.
For a typical patient it acts on, it slightly raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 98% without this part to about 99% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 26 of these 42 patients had heart disease.

A higher ST depression on exercise clearly raises the predicted risk of heart disease, but only if the resting ECG is normal (in an uneven way for patients with a normal resting ECG): for a typical patient, ST depression on exercise going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 18% to about 55% if the resting ECG is normal, and from about 18% to about 18% if resting ECG is something other than a normal resting ECG.
Other effects: ST depression on exercise past about 1.0 mm raises it in an uneven way; a higher ST depression on exercise raises it in an uneven way (on the training data only).
Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: any other resting ECG (rather than a normal resting ECG) lowers it (on the training data only).

ann_32.text: Through this part, maximum heart rate only lowers the predicted risk of heart disease once it rises above about 145 beats per minute: for a typical such patient, going from 71 beats per minute to 182 beats per minute moves it from about 19% to about 13% (on the training data only).
